design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks for one thing — pay out what the savings guarantee owes before the year closes — and names nothing else. The published terms put three problems in front of that payment, each stated only as a waiting clause in the rule of the problem it blocks: the shortfall is worked out only after a signed-off verification of the period's measured savings stands on the record; the verification is worked out only after the baseline has been restated from the close of the retrofit at the building; and the restated baseline is fixed only once the metered points the subscription covers match the points the site meters. None of those three is in the customer's mouth, and one of them — bringing the site's metered points onto the subscription at a higher annual fee — only the owner may authorise, so the agent has to discover it, price it and hand it over mid-call. Every one of the four numbers is a multi-factor computation over a reconciled ledger (twenty-four monthly utility bills, thirty-four interval readings, twelve invoices and their payments, the year's guarantee crediting, last year's true-up and the payment that settled it) plus reads into three other difficulties' products: the retrofit project that closed in March, the automation service plan whose support pool is spent, and the maintenance agreement whose repair allowance is exhausted.

SCOPE (Principle C). Task 0 occupied energy_ext_analyst_overage_charge and energy_ext_subscription_settlement_payment (the analyst-hours pool and ledger settlement, tools charge_analyst_overage_446fe12a and settle_subscription_balance_535836bf). This task claims the remaining four: energy_ext_meter_coverage_amendment, energy_ext_retrofit_baseline_reset, energy_ext_savings_verification and energy_ext_shortfall_settlement, with tools authorise_meter_coverage_01d41e30, reset_performance_baseline_0e66b991, verify_period_savings_a6d7fa6e and pay_savings_shortfall_2f1bc21a. No policy, tool, subject event or computed parameter is shared with task 0: task 0 writes invoice and payment rows under energy_billing_and_late_fee, this task writes coverage, verification and guarantee rows under energy_agg_portfolio_meter_pricing, energy_portfolio_interaction and energy_savings_guarantee. Together the two tasks cover all six extended policies.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: energy_ext_shortfall_settlement (what the caller's request points at). Prerequisites, as a chain: energy_ext_meter_coverage_amendment -> energy_ext_retrofit_baseline_reset -> energy_ext_savings_verification -> energy_ext_shortfall_settlement.
 Edge shortfall <- verification: kind value_input; gate = the compute binding guaranteed_latest; form state; sentence "The shortfall paid against the guarantee is worked out only after a signed-off verification of the measured savings for the true-up period stands on the subscription's record."; condition: the subscription's record carries a signed-off verification for the true-up period with the guaranteed and measured figures on it; resolved by verify_period_savings_a6d7fa6e (agent). Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; the side waited on is a record-visible state (a verification standing on the record), naming no action, performer or tool; no code token; strength exactly "only after", scoped to the true-up period. Exactly one write of this difficulty puts a verification on the record — the verification policy's own target tool.
 Edge verification <- baseline reset: kind value_input; gate = the compute binding baseline_use; form state; sentence "The savings verified for a true-up period are worked out only after the baseline standing on the subscription has been restated from the close of the replacement or retrofit project at the building."; condition: the baseline standing on the subscription is the restated figure and the subscription's last change of coverage is that baseline reset; resolved by reset_performance_baseline_0e66b991 (agent). Only the baseline-reset policy's write restates a baseline on an energy subscription.
 Edge baseline reset <- coverage amendment: kind state_gate; gate energy_subscriptions.meters_covered; form state; sentence "The reset baseline is fixed only once the metered points the subscription covers match the points the site meters."; condition: the metered point count standing on the subscription equals the number of metered points that posted a reading in the month ending on the day of the reset; resolved by authorise_meter_coverage_01d41e30 (owner=user — only the building owner may commit to the higher annual fee). Only the coverage-amendment policy's write changes the covered point count.
 Derivation a reader must perform on each hop: the sentence names a state; the records show it does not hold (no verification for the year; a baseline still stated over 2021-10-01 to 2023-09-30 with the last coverage change a user addition in April; thirty covered points against thirty-four posting readings); the depended-on policy's own rule says what its write books, and it is the only write that books it.
 Why each is false at the opening: initial_state.energy_subscriptions.<sub>.meters_covered = 30 against thirty-four interval readings posted on 2026-09-05; initial_state.energy_subscriptions.<sub>.baseline_kwh = 6480000 with last_change_type users_added and last_change_date 2026-04-14, so no reset has been made since the project closed on 2026-03-20; and the only energy_savings_verified row on the subscription is the 2025 true-up verified on 2025-11-20, so nothing stands for the closing year.
 Topological order: coverage amendment, baseline reset, verification, shortfall settlement. The tree is a chain, so no two writes may be reordered and the terminal state is unambiguous; the two writes that touch the same holding row (the coverage amendment and the baseline reset) are ordered by the reset's own prerequisite sentence, so the last_change stamp is deterministic.
 Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 runs): skipping the verification leaves the shortfall settlement computing on the 2025 true-up instead of the new one; skipping the baseline reset moves the verified savings from 15722.66 to 58272.48 and the payment with it; skipping the coverage amendment leaves the covered point count at thirty and the annual fee at 34000.00 in the terminal state, and the condition the reset waits on unmet.
 user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: the caller names no verification, no baseline, no meter count and no coverage change; he asks only for the guarantee to be settled, says he has not worked anything out, and reacts to the coverage authorisation only after the desk explains it and hands it to him. Tools do not block: each of the four task tools is a single ctx.update or ctx.create with no lookup, no comparison and no policy error, so every one of them writes faithfully whether or not its prerequisite has been resolved.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. The coverage amendment and the baseline reset both write the subject energy_coverage_updated, governed by energy_agg_portfolio_meter_pricing (no structured eligibility; its scope is that the portfolio meter count decides the per-meter step and that each subscription is priced from its own tier's numbers) and energy_portfolio_interaction (whose only gate, retrofit_completion_resets_baseline, applies to energy_savings_verified and so imposes nothing on these two writes; its scope here is that the point licence sits on the automation plan where the data is drawn from it). The verification writes energy_savings_verified, governed by energy_savings_guarantee (its gate verified_shortfall_on_record applies to energy_shortfall_paid, not to this subject) and by energy_portfolio_interaction, whose gate retrofit_completion_resets_baseline does apply: it is satisfied by retrofit_projects.<prj> standing closed with completion_date 2026-03-20 at the same site, correlated to the call's site_id argument. The shortfall payment writes energy_shortfall_paid, governed by energy_savings_guarantee, whose gate verified_shortfall_on_record is satisfied by the verification row this call's own earlier step created, correlated on billing_period and subscription_id. No gate on any of the four subjects is a time gate, so temporal_feasibility is empty.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: the single Measurement & Verification Program subscription at the Cedarhurst Medical Pavilion; the owner holds no second energy subscription and the building has one automation plan, one maintenance agreement and one closed retrofit project, so every cross-category read resolves to exactly one row. The true-up period is the subscription year ending with the term on 2026-09-30, written 2026 in the ledger's own form; last year's true-up (2025, verified 2025-11-20) and the 6750.00 paid against it are the already-settled objects, and they are deliberately inside the twelve-month window so that the shortfall measure's tiers are genuinely different readings of the same ledger. The twenty-four utility bills carry the building's use; the thirty-four interval readings posted on 2026-09-05 are the points the site meters.

SEED — WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW EXISTS. The twenty-four monthly utility bills are the building's use: the first twelve at 560000 kWh and 0.11 a unit, the next six at 545000 and 0.12, the last six at 430000 and 0.12, so the retrofit's effect is visible in the record and the twelve-month and twenty-four-month windows genuinely differ. The thirty-four interval readings posted on 2026-09-05 are the points the site meters, against thirty covered; delete four of them and the coverage amendment, the points-beyond charge and the coverage share all move. The twelve monthly invoices and their eleven payments leave exactly one invoice outstanding, due on the day of the call so that nothing is past due and no late fee or suspension obligation is alive, and give the offset factor its charges and payments. The guarantee crediting of 62000.00 and the analyst-hours crediting are the year's openings; the 2025 verification and the 6750.00 paid against it are last year's settled true-up and the evidence the repeat-payment share rests on. The three performance reports are the year's ordinary reporting. The controls plan, the maintenance agreement and the closed retrofit project are the cross-difficulty evidence four factors read; each is seeded consistently with its own product's charter. guarantee_pool_remaining on the subscription row is deliberately stale at 12000.00 while the ledger nets to 55250.00, and no rule reads it: it is what an agent who trusts the displayed pool instead of the guarantee ledger will use.

PERSONA. Desmond Achebe is written as a clipped, rehearsed complainant: he opens with the company and the callback number, gives the account number and the tax digits when asked to confirm himself, names the building, mentions the two new chillers only when asked what changed, refuses to put a number on what he is owed, and takes the money however the desk normally pays it. He never names a verification, a baseline, a meter count or a coverage change, never asks whether something must be sorted first, and reacts to the authorisation only after the desk explains it and hands it over. His last reaction answers the last gold action — the payment against the guarantee — and asks for nothing beyond it.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION. Everything happens at 2026-09-17 09:40:00 -0500: the account is located and verified from what he states, the subscription, its ledger, the automation plan, the maintenance agreement, the retrofit project and the lodged requests are read, the owner authorises the coverage on the spot, and the reset, the verification and the payment are all synchronous writes. Nothing waits on a visit, a meter installation, a bill, a clearing, a review or a future date; the retrofit closed on 2026-03-20 and the thirty-four meters were posting before the call, both as official records rather than as anything the persona asserts.

DIFFICULTY / EASY MISTAKES. Settling the guarantee straight off the 2025 verification; verifying against the old baseline of 6480000 instead of the restated figure; taking the billed use of the last twelve months as the measured basis instead of the twenty-four months restated as a year; forgetting that the reduction is taken only for the months the new chillers have actually run; valuing the saving at the twenty-four month average unit cost the entry tier uses; missing that the maintenance agreement's repair allowance is exhausted or that the automation plan's support pool is spent; reading guarantee_pool_remaining (12000.00) instead of netting the guarantee ledger; and pricing the coverage amendment off the tier's list fee rather than the escalated fee the renewal window brings.

user_scenario:
Desmond Achebe runs facilities for Cedarhurst Health Partners, and the Medical Pavilion out in Franklin Park is the building that keeps him up at night. He is brisk on the phone, a little clipped, the way someone is when they have been rehearsing a complaint in the car. The subscription year on his energy programme finishes at the end of this month, and what he rings about is the savings guarantee: the company promised a saving on that building and, in his words, his utility spend has not come down anything like the way it was supposed to. He wants the guarantee settled and the money that is owed under it paid out to Cedarhurst now, before the year closes, and he says so plainly at the start. He is content for the desk to work through whatever records it needs and to act for him on the company's side of it, and he is not asking to cancel anything, to renew anything or to change what the programme covers.

He gives the company name, Cedarhurst Health Partners, LP, and the number the desk should call back on, 3125550472, without being asked. When the desk wants him confirmed, he reads the account number from the last invoice, 640751, and then the last four of the federal tax identification number, 4468; the billing address and the accounts email are also his to give if either is asked for, but he leads with those two.

Asked which building, he says the Medical Pavilion in Franklin Park, and that it is the only one on the energy programme. Asked whether anything changed at the building over the year, he says they put two new chillers in over the winter and the work was signed off in the spring, and he leaves it there unless he is asked more. Asked what he thinks he is owed, he says he has not worked it out and does not intend to, that it is the company's figure to produce, and he will not put a number to it. Asked how he wants the money, he says however the desk normally does it, against the account is fine, and he does not ask for a cheque. He has no reference number for the programme or for any invoice and says so if asked.

He does not know how the guarantee is worked out and never proposes a method, a period or an order of doing anything. When the desk tells him that the points the building now meters have to be carried on the programme before the year can be settled, and that it lifts the annual fee, he grumbles that nobody mentioned it when the meters went in, asks whether it is really necessary, accepts the answer he is given and then does the authorisation himself when it is handed to him, using exactly the figures the desk gives him. Told afterwards that the baseline has been restated, or that the year has been verified, he takes both at face value and waits. Once he hears that the payment against the guarantee has been made and what it came to, he says that is what he wanted to hear, thanks the desk for sorting it before the year closed, and rings off.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the whole subscription ledger: the utility bills by month with their consumption and cost, the interval readings posted this month, the invoices and payments, the guarantee crediting, last year's verification and the shortfall paid against it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every aggregate of all four computations is reconciled from these rows, and they are where a reader sees that no verification stands for the closing year and that thirty-four points are posting against thirty covered.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the replacement and retrofit project at the same building: its class, the stage it stands at, its contract value, what it replaced and the day it closed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The contract value, the scope and the closing date decide the retrofit reduction, the equipment share and the running share in the baseline reset, and the year share in the shortfall payment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the building automation service plan at the same building: its standing and the support hours still standing on it for its plan year.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan's standing decides the gateway charge in the amended fee, and its standing with an exhausted support pool decides the system share of the shortfall.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the preventive maintenance agreement at the same building: its standing and the repair allowance still standing on it for the year.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The agreement's standing and its exhausted repair allowance decide the share of the measured saving the verification attributes to the company's work.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read what the owner has lodged on the energy side: the completed site survey, the confirmed quote acceptance and the claim lodged against the guarantee.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The survey and acceptance are what put the subscription at the tier whose guarantee and fees every figure is measured against, and the lodged claim is the record of the demand being answered.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Open the coverage authorisation to the customer and hand it over, since only the owner may commit the account to a higher annual fee.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair for the customer's own write; it changes no record and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The owner takes the thirty-four points the building meters onto the subscription at the restated annual fee, changing the covered point count and the fee standing on the account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: energy_ext_meter_coverage_amendment is the only policy that produces the restated annual fee, and the covered point count it sets is the state the baseline reset waits on.

The fee basis factor: the subscription stands in its renewal window, so the fee the amendment is struck on is the tier's annual subscription fee of 34000 escalated once at the tier's 3 percent escalation, 35020.00. The portfolio band factor: thirty-four covered points stand above the lower band of twenty and at or below the upper band of sixty, so the per-point fee is the tier's 165 less the middle band step of 6 percent, 155.10, and thirty-four points carry 5273.40. The gateway factor: the building's automation service plan stands active and the subscription draws its data from more than one source, so the tier's 480 gateway fee is carried at the shared share, 240.00. 35020.00 + 5273.40 + 468.00 + 819.00 + 240.00 = 41820.40, rounded to the cent once at the end.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, so its topological order is unique and no two writes may be reordered: the coverage authorisation, then the baseline reset, then the verification, then the payment. The two writes that touch the same holding row are ordered by the reset's own prerequisite sentence, so the last change stamped on the subscription is the baseline reset and the terminal state is unambiguous.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the verification leaves the payment struck on the 2025 true-up (guaranteed 48000.00 against verified 39000.00) instead of the closing year's 57791.83 against 15722.66, so the scored payment argument changes from 9475.14 to a figure taken from last year's settled period.
Skipping the baseline reset leaves the verification measuring against 6480000 instead of 6019982: the verified savings move from 15722.66 to 58272.48, and the payment with them.

Skipping the coverage authorisation leaves meters_covered at 30 and annual_subscription_fee_usd at 34000.00 in the terminal state, and leaves the state the reset waits on unmet, so the terminal database differs on the holding row itself.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario names no verification, no baseline, no metered point count and no coverage change, and asks no question about whether something must be settled first: the caller asks only for the guarantee to be settled, refuses to put a figure on it, and mentions the chillers only when he is asked what changed at the building. His part in the coverage authorisation is entirely passive — he grumbles, asks whether it is necessary, accepts the answer and runs the tool once the desk has handed it to him.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Each of the four task tools is one ctx.update or ctx.create with its arguments as declared: reset_performance_baseline_0e66b991 never reads meters_covered, verify_period_savings_a6d7fa6e never looks for a baseline reset, and pay_savings_shortfall_2f1bc21a never looks for a verification. None of them compares, refuses or hints, so each writes faithfully whether or not its prerequisite has been resolved, and the only consequence of skipping one is a different terminal hash.
